clue.text: One helps to get a seat for someone standing

definitions.text: One helps to get a seat for someone standing

parts.words: One helps to get a seat for someone standing
parts.note: reads like a kind passenger giving up a chair on a bus, but 'standing' means running for office and the 'seat' is in parliament; each voter helps put a candidate there

explanation.surface: A courteous commuter offers a seat to someone left standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing' is the misdirection: in British politics a candidate stands for election, and a parliamentary constituency is a seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter casts a ballot that helps a candidate win a parliamentary place.

clue.text: Parrot house south of city

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece south of another is written below it, so it comes second

parts.note: EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: Directions to a bird's home on the southern edge of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: EC (East Central) is the London postcode covering the City, the financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to repeat words mechanically, which is what an echo does with sounds.

clue.text: Resent messenger dropping round

indicators.note: dropping means the round letter is let fall out of the messenger word

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomatic messenger
O is round in shape, so it stands for round

explanation.surface: Someone resents a courier who skips a delivery round.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe begrudging what someone else has, a near-synonym pair.

clue.text: Call for small missile to tip unfavourable balance

indicators.note: to tip something is to upend it, so in this down clue the whole string is turned upside down

parts.note: to page someone is to call them over a speaker system
a dart is a small thrown missile

explanation.surface: A request for a little projectile to tip the scales against someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tip' reverses PAGEDART, giving the answer read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A country's deficit in imports over exports is an adverse balance of commerce.

clue.text: Dish from Agra, it appears

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A dish that seems to come from the Indian city of Agra.
explanation.definitionFit: This yoghurt side dish with cucumber is a staple of Indian meals.

clue.text: Supported DUP, the old leaders having gone

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its leading letter, D, T and O

explanation.surface: The DUP backed something, its former leaders having departed.
explanation.walkthrough: The DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To uphold something is to back or maintain it, so a past-tense synonym fits.

clue.text: Plea from competitor having once changed sides

indicators.note: the left letter (L) swaps to the right letter (R), as a player who changed sides would

parts.note: a player is a competitor in a game

explanation.surface: A plea from a sportsman who once switched teams.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R are the usual abbreviations for left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer is an earnest request or entreaty.

clue.text: Yachtsmen moved by these seasonal tales?

parts.note: Easter is a season of the church year
tales can be untruths, i.e. lies

explanation.surface: Sailors stirred by holiday stories?
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' looks emotional, but sails are pushed along by the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Winds from the east propel boats, so they are what drives yachtsmen along.

clue.text: Criminal should lose accommodation made for his children, maybe

definitions.text: accommodation made for his children, maybe

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A villain loses the home built for his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his children, maybe' are a child's toy figures, for whom the miniature home is made.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy home is a miniature dwelling built for a child's figurines to live in.

clue.text: Almost lose it, as one will with last jigsaw piece

definitions.meaning: to become wildly agitated, nearly losing one's temper

definitions.text: as one will with last jigsaw piece
definitions.meaning: the final piece of a puzzle will slot neatly into its place

explanation.surface: Nearly losing your temper, as anyone would over the final jigsaw piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an outburst of rage and being of the right shape to slot in.

clue.text: Engendering invasion by America of constituent state

indicators.note: invasion means one piece entering another, so America goes inside the state

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, one of the states making up the union
USA is the abbreviation for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A rather sinister account of the US invading one of its own states.
explanation.definitionFit: Something causal brings about an effect, just as engendering produces something.

clue.text: Rent regularly appended to account for lodgings

indicators.note: appended to means added on after the first piece

parts.note: a bill is an account of money owed

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word Rent

explanation.surface: Rent charged regularly is added to the bill for one's rooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A billet is quarters where soldiers are housed, so it is a form of accommodation.

clue.text: Attitude of cynic from Tyneside given seats at random

parts.note: Tyneside is in the north-east of England, abbreviated NE

indicators.note: at random means the letters are mixed up in no fixed order

explanation.surface: A cynic from Newcastle grumbles at being given seats haphazardly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic has a pessimistic, doubting outlook on everything.

clue.text: A Parisienne, fading away when imprisoned, not improving

parts.note: une is French for 'a' in the feminine, as a woman of Paris would say it

indicators.note: imprisoned means the short word is locked inside the longer one

parts.note: fading away can mean dying
if can mean when, as in 'if it rains, stay in'

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman wasting away in jail finds it hardly uplifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something edifying improves the mind morally, so its negative fails to enlighten.

clue.text: Not allowed to enter, being ill (ie poorly)

indicators.note: poorly means in a bad state, so these letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: Someone barred from a competition because they are ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A person disqualified from taking part lacks the right to join or compete.

clue.text: Note on a cross in register: free of charge

indicators.note: in means the short pieces are placed inside the register word

parts.note: a table is a list or register of items
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: An instruction to mark a cross in a ledger to show no fee is due.
explanation.definitionFit: Income exempt from duty attracts no levy, so no payment is charged on it.

clue.text: Apprehension remains after troops turned up

indicators.note: after means the remains come following the troops
in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of troops
the rest is what remains

explanation.surface: Anxiety lingers after soldiers appear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apprehension' looks like worry but is used in its sense of seizing a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehension can mean the capture of a suspect by police, a detention.

clue.text: Toilet water unavailable in station

indicators.note: unavailable means the water part is missing from the station name

parts.note: Waterloo is a major railway terminus in London

explanation.surface: A traveller complains the station lavatory has no running water.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a lavatory.

clue.text: Quick check when finished

parts.note: once can mean as soon as or when, as in 'once you're done'
over means finished

explanation.surface: A quick inspection to be done when the work is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapid, cursory examination of something is a swift look-through.

clue.text: Key was first put in the wrong way

indicators.note: put in the wrong way means the letters are entered backwards

parts.note: to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A key that was inserted first but upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Delete is a key on a computer keyboard, usually labelled with this short form.

clue.text: Would-be rulers not yet loving society?

parts.note: pre means before, i.e. not yet happened
tender means loving and affectionate

explanation.surface: Aspiring monarchs not yet fond of high society?
explanation.definitionFit: Claimants to a throne are people who assert a right to rule.

clue.text: Briskly move coke ashes for building blocks

definitions.meaning: to move along quickly and casually, as in sweeping into a room
cinders from burnt coke, mixed with cement to make lightweight blocks

explanation.surface: Coke ashes being shifted swiftly to make building blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for moving airily and a noun for furnace cinders used in construction.

clue.text: Winter sportsperson in form takes extraordinary run

parts.note: a figure is a form or shape

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An athlete in good shape goes on an exceptional run.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice performer gliding in patterns competes in a cold-season sport.

clue.text: Proceed at leisure, having skill to rake in millions

indicators.note: to rake in is to gather in, so the millions go inside

parts.note: able means skilled, a stand-in for skill
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A wealthy person takes life easy, being clever enough to earn millions.
explanation.walkthrough: ABLE is an adjective clued by the noun 'skill'; read 'having skill' as being able.
explanation.definitionFit: To walk at a slow, relaxed pace is to stroll without hurry.

clue.text: Standard cut by one or two?

indicators.note: cut by means the standard is split open by the other piece

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question of whether a norm is undercut by one or two.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is a set of two.

clue.text: Colour choice

definitions.meaning: used as an adjective for the best, as in a choice job

explanation.definitionFit: The fruit's name is both a purple shade and an adjective for something excellent.

clue.text: Where most are by midnight, assuming resistance is instinctive

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the resistance is taken into the phrase

parts.note: most people are tucked up asleep by midnight
R is the symbol for resistance in physics

explanation.surface: A generalisation that most people turn in by midnight because rest is natural.
explanation.definitionFit: An innate quality is one present from birth, natural rather than learned.

clue.text: Primarily a lovable rogue

indicators.note: rogue means behaving erratically, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Above everything else, a charming scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means most importantly, putting something first.

clue.text: Surgery ultimately stops feminist looking older

indicators.note: stops means the letter plugs a gap inside the feminist's name

parts.note: Germaine Greer is a famous feminist writer

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word Surgery

explanation.surface: A feminist who refused cosmetic surgery now looks her age.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair turning more silver is a sign of age, so the comparative means appearing more aged.

clue.text: East Ender's caught peculiar part of anatomy

indicators.note: a Cockney from London's East End drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: to have heard a remark is to have caught it
rum means odd or peculiar

explanation.surface: A Londoner has picked up a strange bit of body.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from London's East End, traditionally drop the initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: The membrane in the ear that vibrates with sound is a piece of human anatomy.
